title: Why can a cancelled meeting remain in a guest’s calendar?

options.label: Bob’s, a guest at one meeting

answer: a guest’s calendar keeps only the meetings it was sent, and on this server a cancellation marks the guest’s copy CANCELLED instead of deleting it

checks.question: Alice skips the fifth meeting, Monday 30 November, instead of Bob’s, by adding EXDATE:20261130T090000Z. How many meetings does her calendar show, and when is the last? What does Bob’s calendar show?
checks.answer: Alice’s shows five, the last still on Monday 7 December: COUNT=6 counts the excluded start, so the series does not run a week longer. Bob is still in the third meeting’s override, so any update the server sends him carries that override again, and his calendar keeps Monday 16 November, not cancelled.

checks.question: Alice moves the second meeting, which Bob does not attend. Before trying that setting: does Bob’s copy change, and why?
checks.answer: No. The iTIP REQUEST the server sends him holds only the VEVENTs he attends, the third meeting’s override, so his copy keeps that one VEVENT and never learns of the move.

checks.question: Bob’s calendar app wants to show him the rest of the stand-up series. Which lines would it need that his stored copy lacks?
checks.answer: The master’s DTSTART and RRULE. His copy holds one override and no masters, so it has no rule to generate the other weeks from; only the organiser’s object has one.

scenarios.name: Alice’s change: No other change · Whose copy: Alice’s, the organiser

steps.title: A weekly stand-up is stored as one VEVENT
steps.line: DTSTART is the first meeting; RRULE with COUNT=6 makes six.
steps.caption: Alice cancels one meeting of her weekly stand-up. Bob, invited to that meeting alone, can still find it in his calendar, marked cancelled. To see why, start with how Alice’s app stores the series: as one VEVENT, the iCalendar record for an event. DTSTART is the first meeting, Monday 2 November 2026 at 09:00 UTC. RRULE repeats it weekly, and COUNT=6 stops after six meetings, with DTSTART counting as the first. The list shows the meetings a calendar computes from those two lines.
steps.picture: Code “Alice’s stored object, some lines left out”, 5 lines; “Meetings Alice’s calendar shows”, 6 labelled values.

steps.title: Inviting Bob to one meeting stores a second VEVENT
steps.line: Same UID, and RECURRENCE-ID 20261116T090000Z names the third meeting.
steps.caption: Alice invites Bob to the third meeting only. The app keeps the first VEVENT as it was and adds a second with the same UID, an override. Its RECURRENCE-ID, 20261116T090000Z, is the start the rule gave that meeting, kept even if the meeting moves. Bob is sent this override and nothing else. His copy has one occurrence, not the master rule that generates Alice’s whole series.
steps.picture: Code “Alice’s stored object, some lines left out”, 11 lines; “Meetings Alice’s calendar shows”, 6 labelled values. Added: 6: BEGIN:VEVENT; 7: UID:standup; 8: RECURRENCE-ID:20261116T090000Z; the override: Week 3: Mon 16 Nov, 09:00, with Bob; and 3 more.

steps.title: Five meetings come from the rule, one from the override
steps.line: The override replaces the start that equals its RECURRENCE-ID.
steps.caption: Alice changes nothing else, so the object keeps two VEVENTs. A calendar takes all six starts from the rule, then puts the override in place of the start that equals its RECURRENCE-ID. Five meetings come from the first VEVENT and one from the second.
steps.picture: Code “Alice’s stored object, some lines left out”, 11 lines; “Meetings Alice’s calendar shows”, 6 labelled values. The master: 1: BEGIN:VEVENT; 2: UID:standup; 3: DTSTART:20261102T090000Z; and 2 more.

steps.title: Alice’s object holds the rule; Bob’s holds one meeting and no rule
steps.line: Each row is one calendar, over the six weeks of Alice’s rule.
steps.caption: Alice’s object holds the master, whose RRULE gives all six weeks, and the override that puts Bob in the third. Bob’s holds that override and no master, so his calendar shows the third week and no other.
steps.picture: Alice’s stored object. As saved after inviting Bob. Master. RRULE COUNT=6. Override. RECURRENCE-ID 16 Nov, with Bob. Bob’s stored object. iTIP sent to him: REQUEST. Master. none, so no RRULE. Override. RECURRENCE-ID 16 Nov. Alice’s calendar: six meetings. 2. Nov. 9. Nov. 16. Nov. 23. Nov. 30. Nov. 7. Dec. Bob’s calendar: one meeting. 16. Nov.

steps.title: One UID: at most one master, any number of overrides
steps.line: At a line’s end, a bar is one, a circle zero, a crow’s foot many.
steps.caption: The storage rules explain why Bob can keep one occurrence without Alice’s master rule. Marks at a line’s ends say how many: a bar is one, a circle zero, a crow’s foot many. RFC 4791 puts every VEVENT with one UID in one calendar object: the master, which it defines as the one without RECURRENCE-ID, and the overrides, which may be stored without it, as Bob’s is.
steps.picture: ER diagram: 5 entities, 5 relationships.

steps.title: Alice’s copy: two VEVENTs, one UID
steps.line: One master and one override; her calendar shows six meetings.
steps.caption: The server stores Alice’s object as her app saved it: one master with one RRULE and no EXDATEs, and one override, all with UID standup. The notes on the schema count each part, and parts her copy lacks are dimmed. Bob’s copy is different: a guest’s calendar keeps only the meetings it was sent, and on this server a cancellation marks the guest’s copy CANCELLED instead of deleting it.
steps.picture: ER diagram: 5 entities, 5 relationships. Note: “1 master” beside MASTER: DTSTART (datetime); “1 override” beside OVERRIDE: RECURRENCE-ID (datetime), DTSTART (datetime); “1 RRULE” beside RRULE: FREQ (text), COUNT (int); and 1 more.

steps.title: The server refuses a second master or a second RRULE
steps.line: It answers 415, though RFC 5545 says just that RRULE SHOULD NOT repeat.
steps.caption: Baïkal, running sabre/dav, checks each object saved to it and answers 415 to two VEVENTs without RECURRENCE-ID or to two RRULEs in one VEVENT. RFC 5545 recommends against a repeated RRULE, saying it SHOULD NOT occur, but does not forbid it; sabre is stricter, so the RRULE line now allows at most one. Bob’s copy, with no master, is accepted.

scenarios.name: Alice’s change: Skip Bob’s meeting · Whose copy: Alice’s, the organiser

steps.title: A weekly stand-up is stored as one VEVENT
steps.line: DTSTART is the first meeting; RRULE with COUNT=6 makes six.
steps.caption: Alice cancels one meeting of her weekly stand-up. Bob, invited to that meeting alone, can still find it in his calendar, marked cancelled. To see why, start with how Alice’s app stores the series: as one VEVENT, the iCalendar record for an event. DTSTART is the first meeting, Monday 2 November 2026 at 09:00 UTC. RRULE repeats it weekly, and COUNT=6 stops after six meetings, with DTSTART counting as the first. The list shows the meetings a calendar computes from those two lines.
steps.picture: Code “Alice’s stored object, some lines left out”, 5 lines; “Meetings Alice’s calendar shows”, 6 labelled values.

steps.title: Inviting Bob to one meeting stores a second VEVENT
steps.line: Same UID, and RECURRENCE-ID 20261116T090000Z names the third meeting.
steps.caption: Alice invites Bob to the third meeting only. The app keeps the first VEVENT as it was and adds a second with the same UID, an override. Its RECURRENCE-ID, 20261116T090000Z, is the start the rule gave that meeting, kept even if the meeting moves. Bob is sent this override and nothing else. His copy has one occurrence, not the master rule that generates Alice’s whole series.
steps.picture: Code “Alice’s stored object, some lines left out”, 11 lines; “Meetings Alice’s calendar shows”, 6 labelled values. Added: 6: BEGIN:VEVENT; 7: UID:standup; 8: RECURRENCE-ID:20261116T090000Z; the override: Week 3: Mon 16 Nov, 09:00, with Bob; and 3 more.

steps.title: Skipping Bob’s meeting adds an EXDATE; five meetings remain
steps.line: COUNT=6 still counts the excluded start; the override is deleted.
steps.caption: Alice cancels the third meeting. Her app adds EXDATE:20261116T090000Z to the first VEVENT and deletes the override that invited Bob. COUNT=6 still counts the excluded start, because RFC 5545 generates the rule’s starts first and then removes EXDATEs, so five meetings remain.
steps.picture: Code “Alice’s stored object, some lines left out”, 6 lines; “Meetings Alice’s calendar shows”, 6 labelled values. Added: 5: EXDATE:20261116T090000Z; skipped: Week 3: skipped, EXDATE. New in this step: 6: END:VEVENT.

steps.title: Alice’s rule loses a week to EXDATE; Bob has no rule, only that meeting
steps.line: Each row is one calendar, over the six weeks of Alice’s rule.
steps.caption: The same cancellation reaches two different objects. Alice’s holds the master, whose RRULE gives six weeks, so her app takes the third out with EXDATE:20261116T090000Z, leaving five meetings. Bob’s holds the override for 16 Nov and no master. His other five weeks are empty because nothing in his copy generates them, and the iTIP CANCEL marks the one VEVENT he has STATUS:CANCELLED.
steps.picture: Alice’s stored object. Her app adds EXDATE to the master. Master. RRULE COUNT=6, EXDATE 16 Nov. Bob’s stored object. iTIP sent to him: REQUEST, then CANCEL. Master. none, so no RRULE. Override. RECURRENCE-ID 16 Nov, CANCELLED. Alice’s calendar: five meetings. 2. Nov. 9. Nov. 16. Nov. EXDATE. 23. Nov. 30. Nov. 7. Dec. Bob’s calendar: one meeting. 16. Nov. cancelled.

steps.title: One UID: at most one master, any number of overrides
steps.line: At a line’s end, a bar is one, a circle zero, a crow’s foot many.
steps.caption: The storage rules explain why Bob can keep one occurrence without Alice’s master rule. Marks at a line’s ends say how many: a bar is one, a circle zero, a crow’s foot many. RFC 4791 puts every VEVENT with one UID in one calendar object: the master, which it defines as the one without RECURRENCE-ID, and the overrides, which may be stored without it, as Bob’s is.
steps.picture: ER diagram: 5 entities, 5 relationships.

steps.title: Alice’s copy: one VEVENT, one UID
steps.line: One master and no overrides; her calendar shows five meetings.
steps.caption: The server stores Alice’s object as her app saved it: one master with one RRULE and one EXDATE, and no overrides, with UID standup. The notes on the schema count each part, and parts her copy lacks are dimmed. Bob’s copy is different: a guest’s calendar keeps only the meetings it was sent, and on this server a cancellation marks the guest’s copy CANCELLED instead of deleting it.
steps.picture: ER diagram: 5 entities, 5 relationships. Note: “1 master” beside MASTER: DTSTART (datetime); “no override” beside OVERRIDE: RECURRENCE-ID (datetime), DTSTART (datetime); “1 RRULE” beside RRULE: FREQ (text), COUNT (int); and 1 more.

steps.title: The server refuses a second master or a second RRULE
steps.line: It answers 415, though RFC 5545 says just that RRULE SHOULD NOT repeat.
steps.caption: Baïkal, running sabre/dav, checks each object saved to it and answers 415 to two VEVENTs without RECURRENCE-ID or to two RRULEs in one VEVENT. RFC 5545 recommends against a repeated RRULE, saying it SHOULD NOT occur, but does not forbid it; sabre is stricter, so the RRULE line now allows at most one. Bob’s copy, with no master, is accepted.

steps.title: Answer: Bob’s copy keeps the meeting, marked cancelled
steps.line: Delivering the CANCEL sets STATUS:CANCELLED and deletes nothing.
steps.caption: A guest’s calendar keeps only the meetings it was sent, and on this server a cancellation marks the guest’s copy CANCELLED instead of deleting it. Bob is now in no meeting, so the server, Baïkal running sabre/dav, sends him an iTIP CANCEL, the scheduling message that calls a meeting off. Delivering it sets STATUS:CANCELLED on the one VEVENT he holds. Alice’s calendar no longer has a third meeting, because she excluded its start from her rule; Bob had no rule to exclude it from, so his copy still contains Monday 16 November, marked cancelled.
